purpose: Source-grounded research cards and literal parser probes, not a tax gold set or model evaluation.

cards.fact_summary: Hong Kong company combines hospitality-package sales with investment holding, owns 75% of Company-F, and expressly is not a pure equity-holding entity. Hong Kong personnel and an unrelated local provider perform activities; staffing and spending are described without actual amounts.
cards.published_outcome_summary: IRD accepted the proposed economic-substance arrangements for this applicant.
review_questions: Can the extractor retain the non-pure classification rather than infer it from investment holding?
Does it leave undisclosed employee and expenditure amounts unknown?
cards.current_engine_limit: Adequacy remains a human judgement; published acceptance is not a numeric adequacy threshold.

cards.fact_summary: Applicant owns two foreign subsidiaries. F1 operates a substantive factory and benefits from a temporary tax concession. Cash dividends travel through the applicant's foreign account into F2 as new share capital; the arrangement excludes settling Hong Kong business debts.
cards.published_outcome_summary: IRD found no Hong Kong receipt on these facts, and separately accepted participation and qualifying-tax conditions in the stated alternative.
review_questions: Can the extractor preserve the whole bank-account and capital-subscription path?
Can it distinguish a conditional alternative ruling from the actual receipt finding?
cards.current_engine_limit: The existing fact dictionary does not by itself encode the full transaction graph or tax-concession history.

cards.fact_summary: Hong Kong investment-holding applicant has foreign parent entities. It has held 60% of a foreign manufacturer's shares since 1992. Foreign enterprise income tax is 25%, while dividend withholding is 10%; the proposed dividends come from profits after enterprise tax.
cards.published_outcome_summary: IRD recognised MNE and Hong Kong resident status and accepted participation and qualifying-tax treatment for the stated dividend arrangement.
review_questions: Can the extractor keep enterprise tax and withholding tax in separate fields?
Does it refrain from treating 10% withholding alone as failure of the qualifying-tax condition?
cards.current_engine_limit: The current engine lacks a complete subject-to-tax analysis; this card is not an automatically executable tax verdict.

cards.fact_summary: A Hong Kong group member receives shares of a foreign company as a dividend in kind and distributes the shares to its Hong Kong parent the same day. The foreign company has no Hong Kong establishment, operations or assets.
cards.published_outcome_summary: IRD did not regard this in-kind dividend as received in Hong Kong under the specified arrangement.
review_questions: Can the extractor represent a share distribution without inventing a cash remittance?
Can it distinguish entity location from the statutory receipt analysis?
cards.current_engine_limit: Receipt cannot be inferred solely from Hong Kong incorporation; the in-kind transaction needs explicit modelling.
